clue.text: Gradually — by dividing quarter in halves

indicators.note: dividing means the word by is set between the two halves, splitting them apart

parts.note: an American quarter (25 cents) is two bits, so its halves are a bit each
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone explains doing a job gradually by cutting a quarter into halves.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang a quarter dollar is 'two bits', which is what lets 'quarter' split into two halves; 'dividing' says the middle word goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something piece by piece, a little at a time, is doing it gradually.

clue.text: Is love dead? Arrange a separation

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
the late king means the dead king

explanation.surface: A partner asks whether love has died and proposes splitting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set apart, keeping one thing separate from others, which is arranging a separation.

clue.text: Copper-bottom, for example, with this?

parts.note: a pan base clad in copper is a bottom of a cheap common metal

explanation.surface: A question about pans made with copper bottoms.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is a non-precious metal, and a bottom is a base: copper-bottoming a pan is giving it a metal base.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is the standard example of a non-precious metal, the alchemists' opposite of gold.

clue.text: Composer to travel, in a way, on one

parts.note: to bus is to travel, one way of getting about
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A composer travels some way, sitting on a single seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ferruccio BUSONI was an Italian composer and pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferruccio Busoni was an Italian pianist and writer of music, best known for Doktor Faust.

clue.text: Dramatist of average weight supporting poet

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece stands underneath, so the weight words come below the poet

parts.note: Dylan Thomas, the Welsh poet
middle means average, in the middle range
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A playwright of average build holds up a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' puts MIDDLE TON below THOMAS. Thomas Middleton was a Jacobean playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Middleton wrote Jacobean plays such as The Changeling and Women Beware Women.

clue.text: Mechanically repeat an average load of rubbish

parts.note: par is an average or normal level, as in 'up to par'
rot is nonsense, a load of rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtlessly repeats an ordinary load of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words without thought, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: Like a fairly good but not outstanding hand

definitions.text: Like a fairly good but not outstanding hand

parts.words: Like a fairly good but not outstanding hand
parts.note: a decent but ordinary bridge holding, and also one a bidder might choose to let go without bidding

explanation.surface: A card player describes a decent but unremarkable hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairly good means adequate, and in bridge a modest hand is one you might simply pass on.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate or tolerable, and a weak hand at bridge is one to pass with.

clue.text: Nice surroundings

parts.note: Nice is the French city on the Mediterranean coast, and this is the stretch of coast around it

explanation.surface: Someone praises pleasant surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective, but it is the French city; capital letter at the start of a clue hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Riviera is the Mediterranean coastline on which the city of Nice stands.

clue.text: Old roads go over Lake District peaks

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in your go
pike is a word for a peak in the Lake District, as in Scafell Pike

explanation.surface: Old roads climb over the peaks of the English Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous region of northwest England; its summits are often called pikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnpikes were historic toll roads, with a gate where travellers paid.

clue.text: Theatrical performances — two at the Westminster Palace

explanation.surface: A note about shows, and about the Palace of Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre plays to full or thin crowds at each showing, and Parliament meets as the Commons and the Lords.

clue.text: Keep right on producing paper

parts.note: to keep a rule or a holiday is to observe it

explanation.surface: Advice to keep right in order to bring out a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, the oldest in the world.

clue.text: Isle of Man — is at a resort there

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning the letters are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is at a seaside resort on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but reads as re-sort, rearranging MAN IS AT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state off the south coast of the Australian mainland.

clue.text: How 9 seemed to poet on Westminster Bridge

definitions.text: How 9 seemed to poet on Westminster Bridge

parts.words: How 9 seemed to poet on Westminster Bridge
parts.note: Wordsworth's sonnet on Westminster Bridge says the very houses (the answer to 9) seem to be sleeping in the early morning

explanation.surface: A question about how buildings struck a poet on a London bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's 'Composed upon Westminster Bridge' has the line 'Dear God! the very houses seem asleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's dawn city lies still and silent, as if sleeping.

clue.text: Inconclusive female put into dock

indicators.note: without a conclusion, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Bertha is a female name

explanation.surface: An indecisive woman is sent to the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inconclusive' removes the last letter of BERTHA.
explanation.definitionFit: To berth a ship is to bring it to a mooring place in harbour.

clue.text: Such beastly members are in order in US

definitions.text: Such beastly members are in order in US

parts.words: Such beastly members are in order in US
parts.note: members of a friendly society named after an animal, and the same animals found in good order across the American plains

explanation.surface: A remark about animal-named club members being correctly ordered in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Antediluvian Order of Buffaloes is a British fraternal society; bison, the American buffalo, live in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Royal Antediluvian Order are called after the bison, the American wild ox.

clue.text: Stride round London avenue, making casual conversation

indicators.note: round means the stride word goes around the avenue word

parts.note: to stalk is to stride stiffly
The Mall is the avenue leading to Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: Walking around a London avenue while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mall is the ceremonial road in London leading to Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Small talk is light, trivial chat, the sort exchanged at parties.

clue.text: Unfortunate man target for her?

indicators.note: unfortunate letters have been badly treated, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hapless husband is the target of a shrewish wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunate' rearranges MAN TARGET; the whole clue describes the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a scolding, bullying woman, whose hapless husband bears the brunt.

clue.text: Difficult to dispose of, even by aggressive salesmanship?

parts.note: hard means difficult
to sell something is to dispose of it for money

explanation.surface: Goods that are tough to shift even when pushed hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard sell is a pushy, high-pressure sales pitch.

clue.text: Reckless way to deceive Nelson's flag-captain

parts.note: to fool someone is to deceive them
Thomas Hardy was the captain of Nelson's flagship Victory at Trafalgar

explanation.surface: A rash way to trick Nelson's senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiss me, Hardy': Captain Thomas Hardy commanded HMS Victory, Nelson's flagship, at Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means rash, bold without sense.

clue.text: Having made mistake, like gymnast, perhaps

explanation.surface: A gymnast who has slipped up.
explanation.definitionFit: Off beam means mistaken, and a gymnast who falls is literally off the balance beam.

clue.text: Egg on cupboard

explanation.surface: Something about eggs placed on a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge them, and a press is an old word for a cupboard for linen.

clue.text: Port of New Orleans

indicators.note: new letters are made from the old word, so it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A port of the Louisiana city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' looks like the city; 'New' rearranges ORLEANS. Salerno is a port in southern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a harbour city on the Gulf of Salerno in Campania.

clue.text: Head girl added spice

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A head girl adds seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the seed of a tropical tree, grated as a seasoning.

clue.text: King — like chess set in Looking Glass 'ouse

indicators.note: house written with its h dropped, telling us to drop the h in Cockney style

parts.words: like chess set in Looking Glass
parts.note: the chess pieces in Through the Looking-Glass are red and white, so the set is half red

parts.words: like chess set in Looking Glass
parts.note: the other colour of the set, alongside white, gives the second half of the phrase

explanation.surface: A king resembles a chess piece inside Alice's mirror house.
explanation.walkthrough: Carroll's Looking-Glass chess set is red and white, so half red; 'ouse, house with its h dropped Cockney style, says drop the h of HALF, leaving ALF. Alfred the Great was an English king.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was the ninth-century king of Wessex.

clue.text: Praiseworthy backing for island split in two

indicators.note: backing means the words that follow are read in reverse order

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
dual means in two parts

explanation.surface: Support for an island divided into two parts is commendable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns both pieces round as one run, so the island's letters end up at the back of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudable means deserving praise, commendable.

clue.text: Oddly East twice bid nothing — no trump is biddable

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: oddly means arranged in a strange way, so the letters are mixed
twice means the East letter is used two times over

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: A bridge auction: East bids twice and passes, and the no-trump call is easy to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges E, E, BID and O into OBEDIE. 'Biddable' means docile, not a bridge term here.
explanation.definitionFit: Biddable means willing to do as told, docile.

clue.text: Being married to a bore can be so unsatisfying

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: Marriage to a dull person proves unsatisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' is not a dull person but the tidal wave on a river, called an EAGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty, too small to satisfy.

clue.text: Whiskers for a Gilbertian pirate

explanation.surface: Facial hair belonging to a pirate in Gilbert's comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Whiskers is a rat in a Beatrix Potter tale; Samuel is the Pirate King's lieutenant in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter's rat is Samuel Whiskers, and the pirate lieutenant in The Pirates of Penzance bears the same first name.

clue.text: Antigone's false denial

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are disguised in a new order

parts.note: Antigone, the heroine of Greek tragedy, with possessive dropped

explanation.surface: The tragic heroine Antigone tells a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges ANTIGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of denying or contradicting.
